% Pattern: title/amsthm. A title of two kinds, as "Proposition-definition" or
% "Observation / Convention", is of the first; a title as "Rado's criterion for
% one equation" is of the word before "for"; and a wish is a conjecture.
% seen in the gold pilot (set X)
% want pd-1 statement/proposition 1
% want oc-1 statement/fact 2
% want rado-1 statement/criterion -
% want wish-1 conjecture 3
\documentclass{amsart}
\newtheorem{pd}{Proposition-definition}
\newtheorem{oc}[pd]{Observation / Convention}
\newtheorem*{rado}{Rado's criterion for one equation}
\newtheorem{wish}[pd]{Wish}
\begin{document}
\begin{pd} Let a tree be a connected graph with no cycle. Then it has a leaf. \end{pd}
\begin{oc} Each graph here is finite. \end{oc}
\begin{rado} The equation has a monochromatic solution when some coefficients sum to zero. \end{rado}
\begin{wish} Each tree has a short proof. \end{wish}
\end{document}
